dimensions.summary: Explicit browser and Node library entries remain separate from the thin executable adapter, while CLI JSON implements its shipped adapter schema.
The executable resolves every generated registry contract by key or ID and generic validation now applies the same bounded preflight before standalone validators.
The browser surface is 19,756 gzip bytes against 65,536 and installed CLI cold execution is 38.71ms against a 2,000ms cross-platform budget.

File/stdin input is byte-bounded, UTF-8 decoding is fatal, non-files and changed files fail closed, generic validation is resource-guarded, and spawn failures cannot masquerade as passing smoke tests.
CLI results omit payloads, migrated values and input locators; catalog output also removes maintainer source paths and no network, discovery or persistence exists.
Browser-platform bundling and Linux Node ESM/file/stdin execution pass locally; real browser plus Linux, macOS and Windows CI evidence remains pending.
The installed package retains zero runtime dependencies, all validation runs without Graph or the central CLI, and publication/CLI bridges remain prohibited.
All 107 tests pass with every tested JSON CLI result validated against the shipped strict schema and repeated catalog output remaining identical.
The compatibility command preserves current/previous negotiation semantics, reports migration and loss metadata, and never returns the migrated payload.
Usage, malformed JSON, unsupported contracts, invalid artifacts, interrupted reads and validator cancellation map to deterministic JSON and exit codes 1, 3 or 130.
The pure CLI application is port-driven and unit-tested separately from the Node adapter, while canonical documentation and machine governance describe one aligned surface.
A real 49-file tarball installs with lifecycle scripts disabled, imports every public subpath, executes the installed binary matrix and stays under 58,284 of 163,840 compressed bytes.
